chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

Allah has made belief obligatory as a purification from polytheism, and prayer as a glorification free from arrogance, and alms-tax as a means of providing sustenance, and fasting as a trial for the sincerity of the people, and pilgrimage as a means of drawing near to religion, and jihad as a source of honor for Islam, and enjoining good as a benefit for the common people, and forbidding evil as a restraint for the foolish, and maintaining kinship as a means of increasing numbers, and retribution as a containment of bloodshed, and establishing the limits as a way of honoring the prohibitions, and abstaining from drinking wine as a protection for the intellect, and avoiding theft as a means of ensuring chastity, and abstaining from adultery as a protection for lineage, and abstaining from sodomy as a means of increasing progeny, and testimonies as a means of overpowering contentions, and abstaining from lying as an honor for truth, and peace as a security from fears, and trustworthiness as an order for the community, and obedience as a glorification of the Imamate.
ai.seo_question: What is the wisdom behind the five pillars of Islam according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This passage from Nahj al-Balagha exemplifies the Shia concept of *hikmah* (divine wisdom) behind *ahkam* (jurisprudence), where Imam Ali (AS) elucidates the metaphysical and sociological objectives of each pillar. By linking rituals like prayer to the purification of ego and social duties like *zakat* to sustenance, the text underscores the holistic integration of individual spirituality with communal stability in Islamic governance.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 252. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:

Allāh has laid down īmān (belief) for purification from polytheism; ṣalāt (prayer) for purification from vanity; zakāt (levy) as a means of livelihood; ṣiyām (fasting) as a trial of the people; ḥajj (pilgrimage to the House of Allāh in Mecca) as a support for religion; jihād (fighting in the way of Allāh) for the honour of Islam; persuasion for good (al-amr bi’l-ma‘rūf ) for the good of the common people; dissuasion from evil (an-nahy ‘ani’l-munkar) for the control of the mischievous; regard for kinship for increase of number; revenge for stoppage of bloodshed; the award of penalties for the realization of importance of the prohibitions; the abstinence from drinking wine for protection of the wit; the avoidance of theft for inculcating chastity; abstinence from adultery for safeguarding descent; abstinence from sodomy for increase of progeny; tendering evidence for furnishing proof against contentions; abstinence from the lie for increasing esteem for truth; maintenance of peace (salām) for protection from danger; imāmah or Imāmate (Divine Leadership) for the orderliness of the community and obedience (to Imāms) as a mark of respect to the Imāmate. [1]
